# Home Note

The Home note is Nick Milo's north-star note: the base you return to and the launchpad into your Maps of Content. It keeps the whole system organized. Together with MOCs it forms the core of the Linking Your Thinking (LYT) framework.

## Setting it up
Milo's basic steps:
1. Open the kit's Home note, read its links and ask which categories relate to you.
2. Click through the links to get familiar, noticing that you can always get back to Home, or to a map and then Home.
3. Pick a subject you already have notes on and start linking your own notes to that MOC.
4. Customize that MOC.

Advanced: edit the links on the Home note to suit you. Less is more at the start, and a bulleted list is faster to maintain than a complicated table. Break things and rearrange until it works. The structure serves you; you can write thousands of notes without opening Home.

## How many MOCs
Home MOCs should be broad. Start with two or three and try to stay below about ten. They are easy to rename or change.

## Version history
Kit 7 gave the Home note 16 maps; Ideaverse Lite 1.0 introduced a Home note with ACE head spaces; version 1.5 added a simpler alternative called Home Basic. See Ideaverse Lite (kit).

## Why it helps
Milo says a trusted Home note and maps let him return to a library after months away without anxiety, and the stable top-of-sidebar maps work as a spatial constellation that aids memory. See Fluid Frameworks (LYT).
